Python for SysAdmins & DevOps engineers

A practical manual that teaches Python 3 through the work you already do: reading logs and configs, running commands, checking disks and ports, and turning one-off shell hacks into real tools.

Hands-on

Practice on a real Linux box, right in your browser

Reading about subprocess is not the same as killing a process. Every chapter is meant to be typed and run. The free iximiuz Labs Python Playground gives you a disposable VM where breaking things is part of the lesson.

Linux VM · sudolatest Python 3uv · pyenvDockerVS Codeno paywall
  1. Open the playgroundSign in to iximiuz Labs and click Start playground. It boots in seconds.
  2. Clone this guideAll the example scripts come with it.
  3. Run, break, fixFollow a chapter and run each script as you go.

The manual

14 chapters, from stdin to sockets

Each chapter teaches one module through a real task and ends with exercises. Read them in order, or jump to what you need today.

Getting Started

  • 01Set Up Your LabA free Linux VM in your browser, or Python on your own machine.
  • 02Standard Input, Output and Errorstdin, stdout, stderr and writing scripts that work in pipelines.
  • 03Working with Filesopen(), with, pathlib and fileinput for configs and logs.
  • 04Command-line Argumentssys.argv, exit codes and a tiny grep.

Standard Library

  • 05The os ModuleEnvironment variables, directories, os.walk and system info.
  • 06The sys ModuleInterpreter info, version checks and why exit codes matter.
  • 07shutil and globCopy, move, archive, check disk usage and match wildcards.
  • 08Date and TimeDurations, UTC, time zones and pruning old backups.
  • 09Running Commands with subprocesssubprocess.run(), capturing output, errors and streaming.
  • 10Building CLIs with argparseFlags, defaults, --help and subcommands for real tools.

Data and Networking

  • 11Working with JSONParse API, kubectl and docker output; call a JSON API.
  • 12Working with CSVInventories and reports with csv.DictReader and DictWriter.
  • 13SQLite: a Database in a FileA zero-setup SQL database for inventories and job history.
  • 14Network Checks with socketPort checks, DNS lookups and parallel sweeps.
Highly recommended

Stuck? Learn it step by step with AI

AI tools love to answer with a wall of text. The free /step-by-step Claude skill fixes that: it explains any topic one short, simple sentence at a time, and waits for you to say "understood" before moving on. It's the closest thing to a patient mentor sitting next to you.

git clone https://github.com/tuladhar/my-claude-skills-as-devops-engineer.git /tmp/skills && cp -r /tmp/skills/skills/step-by-step ~/.claude/skills/

Then open Claude Code and type /step-by-step followed by any topic from this guide.

Get the skill ↗★ Star it if it helps
/step-by-step how subprocess.run captures stdout and the exit code
Step 1. subprocess.run() starts a program and waits for it to finish.
Reply "understood" to continue.
understood
Step 2. It returns a CompletedProcess object that holds the result.
understood
Step 3. The exit code is in result.returncode, where 0 means success.
understood
Step 4. Add capture_output=True and text=True to get the output as a string in result.stdout.

Community driven

This guide is written by people like you

Know logging inside out? Automate switches with netmiko? Write the chapter you wish you had when you started. Merged chapters appear on this site automatically, with your name in the history.

Help wanted

Pick a topic to claim it. It opens a GitHub issue so nobody duplicates your work.

  • + Regular Expressions re
  • + Logging logging
  • + Compression and Archives gzip, tarfile, zipfile
  • + XML with ElementTree xml.etree
  • + Platform Information platform
  • + Signals signal
  • + IP Addresses and Networks ipaddress
  • + Concurrency concurrent.futures, asyncio
  • + HTTP APIs urllib, requests, httpx
  • + SSH Automation paramiko, fabric
  • + System Metrics psutil
  • + Network Devices netmiko
  • + Cloud Automation boto3

  • + Testing Your Scripts pytest

Three ways to help

  1. Fix what you findEvery chapter has an "Edit this page on GitHub" link. Typos and outdated examples count.
  2. Write a chapterMarkdown plus runnable scripts in examples/. The guide explains the style.
  3. Record a GIFA 20-second demo in the playground helps beginners more than a page of text.
